newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to boost private infrastructure investment.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to boost private infrastructure investment.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Monday it would expand loans for private-sector infrastructure developers and allow them to issue longer-term bonds by the end of 1997.

The move was part of measures to boost private-sector investment in the nation's infrastructure construction plan involving 25 projects worth a total of 27 trillion won. These projects were scheduled to begin between 1995 and 1996.
The ministry said in a statement private firms participating in a project worth 500 billion won or more would be allowed to borrow from the state-run Korea Development Bank.
Currently, companies involved in projects worth one trillion won or more are allowed to borrow from the bank.
The ministry said loans for land purchase, which are at present banned, would be allowed if private companies were investing in large-scale projects such as road, port and railway construction.
Private developers would also be allowed to issue bonds with a maturity of more than 12 years, the ministry said.
Bonds with a maturity of five years or less accounted for 94 percent of total bond issues in 1995, the ministry added.
South Korea has said its industrial competitiveness was being eroded by rising transportation costs which stem from poor investment in infrastructure construction in the past.
